_notes: Hulls define slots/base stats (placeholder numbers for balancing). Classes are faction templates on a hull. era = the starting era a class first enters service; it stays available in later eras of the same timeline (kelvin is its own timeline). source: canon/beta/original. A hull's crew is the canon complement (lore only); a class's crew_cost is what building it takes from the crew resource. role (rules.json roles; none = combat) says what a class is for; civilian roles (freighter, colony, construction, science, mining, tanker, courier) mark the civilian and support fleet. Every class ends with cost, build_seconds, crew_cost and requires_tech (a tech_tree.json id, null = starter hull; the Borg, who never research, have requires_tech null and requires_assimilated instead), derived from hull size and role by the formula in rules.json _notes_costing and written by tools/ship_costs.py --write. Formula in short (s = hull size, m = the role's multipliers): duranium 30·s², tritanium 12·s², dilithium 6·s from size 2, parasteel 20·(s−3) above size 3, warp coils 5·(s−4) above size 4, all × m.cost (Borg: dilithium → nanoprobes ×2); build_seconds (20 + 15·s^1.5) × m.build; crew_cost 2·√(hull crew) × m.crew (1 to the hull's crew); tech gate by hull band (size 3 → tier 1, 4 → 2, 5–6 → 3, 8 → 4; sizes 1–2 none) capped at the class's era tech_cap_tier: warp_5, warp_8, warp_9_9, ablative_armor (Borg: deflector_shields, tractor_beam, regenerative_shields, transwarp_conduits); science ships need long_range_sensors. Mark a hand-balanced class "tuned": true to keep its numbers.
